recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for the current core build. If a future work group decision reintroduces an active patient-context molecular sequence resource, evaluate that new artifact directly rather than carrying forward the retired MolecularSequence focus element.
issue_request: FHIR-39110 was Published as Persuasive for R5 and requested a new MolecularSequence.focus element, 0..* Reference(Any), summary=true, to identify the actual focus of a molecular sequence when the focus is not the patient of record, such as trio testing where the subject is the proband and the focus is a parent.
initial_application: The issue was applied before this reconciliation by commit 47b93eae3d/PR #2678, which added MolecularSequence.focus to source/molecularsequence/structuredefinition-MolecularSequence.xml, added a MolecularSequence-focus search parameter, and added a focus example. Merge commit 5eaf750128 brought that implementation into the main history.
additional_context: Later R6 work changed the artifact family. FHIR-51227 was Applied as Persuasive with Modification to replace the legacy MolecularSequence resource with MolecularDefinition and to decouple molecular definitional data from patient/encounter context, leaving patient-specific context to Observation references. Current source/fhir.ini does not list MolecularSequence in active [resources], source/molecularsequence is absent, diagnostics-module text says MolecularSequence has been replaced by MolecularDefinition, and MolecularDefinition.representation.focus is a different CodeableConcept used for representation disambiguation rather than the R5 patient-context Reference focus.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Re-adding MolecularSequence.focus would target retired, out-of-build source, while moving the old focus semantics to MolecularDefinition would contradict the later approved design that keeps patient/encounter context on Observation.
